caption: One swap piston on the bedrock, facing sideways; a stone diagonally above it, powered by an observer that watches the clock's redstone block; a 4-block clock (sticky piston, redstone block, observer, and a lamp you place last to start it) and three redstone dust. Every move of the redstone block arms the swap piston for one game tick, every 6 ticks: lie under the trapdoor, look up at the piston's side and press Attack and Use (one key).

Two bedrock side by side: a swap piston on each (facing out), each with its own stone and observer; the clock's redstone block slides behind the two observers, each watching one of its two cells. Press each piston from its own trapdoor spot.

Three bedrock side by side: the end pistons face out, the middle one faces up; each has its own stone and observer; the clock's redstone block slides behind the first two observers and the clock line runs on a block behind the third. Press each piston from its own trapdoor spot.
Four bedrock side by side: the end pistons face out, the middle ones face up, one stone and observer each; the clock line continues on blocks behind the observers (6 blocks per extra bedrock).
Five bedrock side by side: the end pistons face out, the middle ones face up, one stone and observer each; the clock line continues on blocks behind the observers (6 blocks per extra bedrock).
Eight bedrock side by side: the end pistons face out, the middle ones face up, one stone and observer each; the clock line continues on blocks behind the observers (6 blocks per extra bedrock).
Fifteen bedrock side by side, the longest one clock drives (the clock line's signal reaches 15 blocks): the end pistons face out, the middle ones face up, one stone and observer each.
